subject.title: fix(agents): terminate mixed tool-call batches on critical loop veto

question: After a critical tool-loop veto ends the current run, should already accepted steering and follow-up messages be preserved for the next explicit run or discarded with an explicit user-visible notice?
rationale: The callback executes before queue polling, and the patch's comment, proof, and recovery story disagree; code review cannot choose retention and delivery semantics for accepted user input.

options.title: Preserve for next run
options.body: Keep accepted messages queued, define when the next explicit turn consumes them, and prove none are silently lost or replayed unexpectedly.

options.title: Discard with notice
options.body: Clear the queues on critical termination and surface an explicit terminal message identifying that accepted inputs were not processed.

recommendation.title: Preserve for next run
recommendation.body: Keep accepted messages queued, define when the next explicit turn consumes them, and prove none are silently lost or replayed unexpectedly.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent work on embedded run liveness and terminal outcomes makes this the strongest available routing candidate for the run-ending and queued-input contract.
